why.shell.b_mark_pnt_tables.103: Arithmetics Hard (cc_lev_5, 12 examples) with the test prices of the code change (+800 per answer, −600 per mistake, −70 per second). Now 32 % of novice attempts end at raw 0 (the game clamps the score at 0) and the marks are 20 / 54 / 80 / 93. New marks: 25 / 50 / 80 / 94, novices at raw 0 in 1.5 % of attempts.
why.cc_sp_show_results: Arithmetics has no sp_ prices: cc_show_results is shared with training Hard, so a test-only price needs the one-line code change (the test reads cc_sp_show_results, like the sp_ keys of Guess Who and Numbers). +800 per answer (was 650) removes the clamp at 0 for novices (32 % → 1.5 % of attempts); −600 per mistake (was −900; 8.6 s at 70 per second) keeps fast sloppy typing unprofitable while cutting the mistakes' share of the noise. SEM of the mark 11.9 → 9.2 points. Training is not affected. Without the code change keep cc_show_results and table 103 from tables_if_conditions_unchanged; the simulator warns when cc_sp_show_results is in the config but js/games/arithmetics.js does not read it.
why.cc_lev_1.m_Ops: Medium operation mix + + + − − − × ÷ instead of + − × (the generator draws from this list uniformly, so repeats are weights). Owner's reference for Medium: carrying appears (55 − 28), numbers approach 100, multiplication is rare, maybe division. Real generator, 3000 chains (tools/analysis/train_balance_arithmetics.mjs --content): now + 35 %, − 48 %, × 17 % (3.4 per game, always a two-digit number times 2–9), no ÷; proposed + 40 %, − 41 %, × 9 %, ÷ 9 % (about two of each per game). Carrying stays in 34 % of the examples (39 % of +, 44 % of −), the second number of + and − stays 11 or more, the range 10–99. Work per example 4.77 → 4.90 units, the average player 3.5 → 3.6 s per example. Easy (10–60, + −, no carrying, a third of the second numbers one-digit) and Hard (15–150: a number above 100 in 74 % of the examples, carrying in 65 % of + and 72 % of −, × 16 %, ÷ 15 %) already match the reference. Without division: "7 0 0 0 1 1 1 2" gives × 10 %.
why.cc_show_results.i1_points_arr: Training Hard: 800 per right answer (was 650, the same as Medium, although a Hard example takes the average player 4.8 s against 3.6 s and the game has 30 examples instead of 20). With 650 / −900 / −70 time took 52 % and mistakes 14 % of the Hard maximum: the average player's mean score was 6660 on Hard against 6945 on Medium, the novice's 1364 against 3660 — Hard paid less than Medium. With 800 / −600 / −70 (the prices of the test, cc_sp_show_results) the mean rises on every step: novice 1107 / 3349 / 5504, average 2873 / 6768 / 12026 (Hard = 1.78 × Medium), strong 4565 / 9499 / 17345 (model of tools/analysis/train_balance_arithmetics.mjs: work units of every generated example, players calibrated on the test level to 6 / 4 / 2.5 s per example and 2 / 1 / 0.2 mistakes, pace of a game CV 25 %). A Hard game without mistakes beats the average player's typical Medium game up to 8.2 s per example, 1.7 × slower than his usual pace. Easy and Medium prices are unchanged; the test reads cc_sp_show_results and is not affected.
why.cc_show_results.i2_points_arr: Training Hard: −600 per wrong answer (was −900), as in the test. The average player makes 3.1 mistakes in the 30 Hard examples (1.5 in the 20 of Medium): at −900 they took 2800 points, 14 % of the maximum against 8 % on Medium; at −600 they take 1900 = 8 % of 24000. A mistake still costs as much as 8.6 s plus the time of the second try, so guessing does not pay. Easy (−500) and Medium (−750) are unchanged.
why.MG_connected_calc_med.level_up_param: 3.6 targets (docs/analytics/medium-levels.md: medium — novice 35–45 % of games, average ≥ 85 %): up 6600 → 4000 = 6.4 s per example without mistakes (was 4.6 s; one mistake = 10.7 s). Novice 8 → 41 %, average 59 → 93 %, strong 100 %; games for the 5 steps (median): novice 59 → 12, average 8 → 5. Games under down (1600): average 1 %, novice 26 %. why.MG_connected_calc_hard.level_up_param: up 9000 → 14000 with the Hard prices 800 / −600 / −70 (without mistakes 4.76 s per example; the average player's pace with second tries is 4.8 s). Average 27 % of games (target 20–30 %; median 35 games for the 10 steps), novice 1 %, strong 96 % (target 75–90 % is not reachable together with the average's: the strong player is 1.6 × faster and makes 4 × fewer mistakes; 15000 gives strong 90 % and average 15 %). Games under down (5600): average 3 %, novice 50 %. 3.12.3 lowered it to 12500 and 3.12.4 put 14000 back (owner: the top level is for growing, a step that a player reaches now and then is the reason to train; a strong player who passes it on a good day should not close it quickly): 12500 gave the model average 48 % of the games, outside the 20–30 % target.
why.cc_show_results.i3_points_arr: Easy −60 → −40 per second (medium and hard stay −70; the test has its own cc_sp_show_results). Easy is the level where time eats most of the reward: −60 per second against 350 per answer takes 50 % of the maximum from the average player, and the novice (4.3 s per example, 2.2 mistakes) ends 29 % of his Easy games with 0 points. With −40 per second on Easy the novice ends 4 % at 0; means novice 2498 / 3349 / 5504, average 4040 / 6768 / 12026 still rise. up 2700 then gives novice 47 %, average 92 %. 3.12.3 tried −30 (8.33 s per example) and 3.12.4 put −40 back: with −30 the novice passed 89 % of the Easy games (target 60–75 %, owner: a complete beginner should win often, not always). The 6.25 s per example of Easy is not a faster pace than the 6.43 s of Medium: an Easy example is about a fifth less work (no carry, numbers to 60, only + and −), and the novice passes Easy 68 % against Medium 41 %.
